newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to lend 15.25 billion yen to Bangladesh.
newsitem.headline: Japan to lend 15.25 billion yen to Bangladesh.

text.p: Japan said it will provide 15.25 billion yen in loans to Bangladesh, but took a more cautious stance on whether to extend aid for Bangladesh's plan to develop the Ganges basin.

The decision to grant the yen loans was conveyed by Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka in a meeting with his Bangladeshi counterpart Shah Kibria, held on the sidelines of the Asian Development Bank's (ADB) 30th annual meeting, a Japanese finance ministry official said.
But Mitsuzuka stopped short of pledging Japanese aid to Bangladesh's plan to develop the southern part of the Ganges River.
"Japan will consider the issue on a long-term basis after the World Bank and the ADB first take the initiative," the official quoted Mitsuzuka as saying.
The official said Bangladesh planned to develop the Ganges River as disputes with neighbouring India over water rights have been settled.
Kibria said he appreciated Tokyo's assistance and said the Bangladesh economy was likely to post growth of six percent in fiscal year 1996.
